features: Updated kits fix CPS+ CD-audio discovery, accept single-image Final Fight CD BIN/CUE sources and stop rejecting valid Arrange builds because of README differences.
Upper prepares its Python packages on Linux x86-64 and ARM64 with Python 3.12. Upper, CPS+ and NG+ no longer install unused image libraries.
When your selected game has no output for the chosen platform or region, the builder explains which choices are available.

Point it at your ROM and media folders. Loose files, ZIPs and 7z archives are identified by content, without renaming them. Supported discs and audio can use equivalent containers and lossless formats.
Choose individual games, platforms and regions, or keep everything selected to include future catalog additions.

Check requirements without unpacking ROMs. Disc messages explain absent, unsupported and unmatched images; reports include candidate filenames and sizes. Ready games can update while others wait for missing media.
Reuses verified inputs during a build and skips media scans when the selected outputs are already current, reducing repeated reads from network storage.
Required patches, helpers and Python packages are downloaded and prepared privately when needed.
Run it again to pick up catalog updates. Completed output is grouped by platform, ready to copy.
requirements: Install Python first. Use Python 3.12 on an Apple Silicon Mac or x64 Python 3.13 on Windows for the full catalog. Windows ARM users can use x64 Python 3.13. Python 3.13 from the Microsoft Store is supported on Windows.

On Linux x86-64 or ARM64, use Python 3.12 with venv support, glibc 2.28 or newer and the standard C++ runtime (libstdc++6 on Ubuntu/Debian). Keep the state/cache folder on local storage; your ROM and media folders can be on network storage. The launcher itself requires Python 3.10 or newer; other interpreter combinations may leave some targets unsupported.
You need your own canonical MAME-format arcade ROMs. Some games also need discs, firmware or other media. ArcadePatches names what is missing; it does not download source ROMs or private keys.
On Windows, keep the tool's state/cache folder on a local NTFS disk.
steps: Extract the download and open a terminal in that folder. Launch it with the command for your system below.
Enter your ROM/media folders and an export folder. All games, platforms and regions are selected initially; option 2 lets you narrow them.

Choose Build (shown as Update after your first completed build). It checks your media and builds the ready games; a separate requirements check is optional. Follow the instructions for anything missing.

Read INSTALL.txt in the export folder and copy the platform folders to your device or emulator setup. Later launches check for new releases without scanning your ROM folders; choose Update when you want them.
summary: Build and update your Arcade Patches collection from media you own. Choose your games, platforms and regions, then copy the completed folders to your setup.
title: ArcadePatches
